title.es: Guía de una fiesta para visitantes

es: Explicar una fiesta a visitantes combinando normas, consejos, comparaciones matizadas y generalizaciones prudentes.

teaching.en: Visitors are supposed to respect the quiet time at noon.
teaching.es: Los visitantes deben respetar la hora de silencio del mediodía.
teaching.explanationEs: Are supposed to + verbo: la norma que se espera de los visitantes.
teaching.audioText: Visitors are supposed to respect the quiet time at noon.

teaching.en: My advice is to dress warmly, because the evening parade is noticeably colder.
teaching.es: Mi consejo es que te abrigues, porque el desfile de la tarde es claramente más frío.
teaching.explanationEs: My advice is to + verbo base: consejo directo pero cortés.
segments: My advice is to dress warmly, because
the evening parade is noticeably colder.
teaching.audioText: My advice is to dress warmly, because the evening parade is noticeably colder.

teaching.en: Locals tend to queue patiently for food, so please do not jump the line.
teaching.es: La gente del lugar suele hacer cola con paciencia para comer, así que por favor no te cueles.
teaching.explanationEs: Tend to describe lo que suele ocurrir sin generalizar a todos.
segments: Locals tend to queue patiently for food,
so please do not jump the line.
teaching.audioText: Locals tend to queue patiently for food, so please do not jump the line.

teaching.en: The fair is nowhere near as crowded as the parade, so it is worth a visit in the morning.
teaching.es: La feria no está ni de lejos tan concurrida como el desfile, así que vale la pena visitarla por la mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: Nowhere near as… as compara; it is worth + sustantivo o -ing recomienda.
segments: The fair is nowhere near as crowded as the parade,
so it is worth a visit in the morning.

teaching.en: Check the schedule first, because the parade sometimes starts late.
teaching.es: Mira primero el horario, porque el desfile a veces empieza tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Sometimes matiza: no dices que siempre empiece tarde.
teaching.audioText: Check the schedule first, because the parade sometimes starts late.

teaching.en: If you are not sure, ask at a stall before you join a dance.
teaching.es: Si no estás seguro, pregunta en un puesto antes de unirte a un baile.
teaching.explanationEs: Una guía también orienta: qué hacer cuando tienes una duda.

prompt.es: Escribe una guía breve para visitantes: normas, consejos, comparación y respuesta.

answer.text: Welcome to the harvest fair! Visitors are supposed to respect the quiet time at noon, and it is customary to queue for food. My advice is to dress warmly and wear comfortable shoes, because the evening is much colder. The fair is nowhere near as crowded as the spring parade, so the morning is the best time to visit. Also, avoid taking photos of people without asking. Many visitors ask whether they should bring a gift to a family stall. It is not customary, but people tend to buy something from the stall instead, and the families usually appreciate it. If you are not sure about anything, ask a local. Enjoy the fair!
accepted: Welcome to the harvest fair! Visitors are supposed to respect the quiet time at noon, and it is customary to queue for food. My advice is to dress warmly and wear comfortable shoes, because the evening is much colder. The fair is nowhere near as crowded as the spring parade, so the morning is the best time to visit. Also, avoid taking photos of people without asking. Many visitors ask whether they should bring a gift to a family stall. It is not customary, but people tend to buy something from the stall instead, and the families usually appreciate it. If you are not sure about anything, ask a local. Enjoy the fair!

Hello, visitors! Here is a short guide to our harvest fair. You are supposed to be quiet at noon, and locals tend to queue patiently for food. I suggest that you dress warmly, because the evening is far colder than the afternoon. It is worth going in the morning, since the fair is nowhere near as crowded as the parade. Some visitors ask if they should give a gift to a family stall. That is not customary, but buying something is a nice way to say thank you. If you have any doubt, please ask at the information stall.

Welcome! Please respect the quiet time at noon, as visitors are supposed to. My advice is to arrive early and to check the schedule, because the parade sometimes starts late. The fair is much smaller than the parade, so it is not quite as noisy and you can talk easily. Do you need to bring a gift to a family stall? Not really: it is not expected, but people tend to buy a little food from the stall. Generally, locals are happy to help, so do not be shy and ask. I hope you enjoy the fair.

feedback.es: La guía fija normas con be supposed to, da consejos, compara la feria con el desfile y responde con tacto a la duda sobre el regalo.

origin.text: Fiesta: la feria de la cosecha de Tom. Normas: silencio a mediodía y hacer cola para la comida. Consejos: abrigarse, llevar calzado cómodo, ir por la mañana, no hacer fotos a personas sin preguntar. Comparación: muchísima menos gente que el desfile de primavera. Duda de una visitante: «¿Debo llevar un regalo a un puesto familiar?» (respuesta: no es costumbre, pero mucha gente compra algo). Escribe entre 90 y 140 palabras.
